title: How is a file made?
question: open() with O_CREAT makes a file that is not there. What does the kernel make? (In memory: ramfs.)
text: open() with O_CREAT makes a file that is not there. What does the kernel make?

The path walk reaches "new.txt" and finds no such name; with O_CREAT, [lookup_open](1:lookup_open) asks the file system to make it. In ramfs, [ramfs_mknod](1:ramfs_mknod) makes two things: a new inode, which is the file itself (its mode, its size, its pages), and a name for it in the directory, a dentry pointing at that inode.
Then the open goes on as any open: a `struct file`, a slot in the fd table, and the call returns the fd. [The objects it made and changed](1:ramfs_mknod:objects) are on the right.

Try: [create the same file twice](try:1): the second time the name is there, so `lookup_open` takes the other branch and nothing is made. [With O_EXCL](try:2) the second open fails with EEXIST instead.
tries: int fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/new.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, 0644); close(fd); fd2 = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/new.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, 0644); close(fd2)
int fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/new.txt", O_CREAT | O_WRONLY, 0644); close(fd); openat(AT_FDCWD, "/new.txt", O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY, 0644)
